suggestions.title: Weigh in the morning, not at night — you did step on the scale yesterday and the app binned it

rationale.science: A single reading is noise around a slow trend, so the trend only works if the readings are taken under the same conditions each time; overnight fluid and food shifts are exactly the confound a fixed morning window removes (Article III; DASH-Sodium / Juraschek 2020 on how much water alone moves the number).
rationale.data: Your last clean, usable morning read is 8/6 at 162.8 — five days ago. Since then: 8/8 read filed evening and set aside, 8/9 morning read flagged for salt, 8/10 read filed evening and set aside. On 8/10 the ledger recorded both MORNING READ MISSED (priced at 0.02 lb/wk of rate precision) and a discarded evening read on the same day.
rationale.relationship: You are not skipping the scale — you are weighing at the wrong end of the day, which is a different problem with a different fix. Every rate number in front of you right now (your app's 1.15/wk, the engine's 0.80/wk) is extrapolating from that one 8/6 morning, which is why the two disagree.

suggestions.predict: One in-window morning read tomorrow re-anchors the trend and closes the gap between the two rate figures. I expect it to land 162.8–163.6 if the four maintenance days cost what I think they did. Grade it on reads gaining an 8/12 entry with offWindow absent, and on the app's rate moving off 1.15.

suggestions.title: Press: next upper day, either give the fourth set an honest set or run three — Sunday's best press scored nothing

apply.to: Press 250 next upper day: run 3 working sets, or run 4 with the fourth taken to 1-2 reps in reserve like the first three. Do not repeat 8,8,7 plus a 4-rep tail.

rationale.science: On a cut you defend load rather than chase volume, and a set taken far short of failure adds fatigue without adding the stimulus that justifies it (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024; Grgic 2021).
rationale.data: 250 x 8,8,7 drew PRESS — TARGET MET on 8/6. The identical top three plus a fourth set at 4 reps on 8/9 drew no press feed row at all, while rows, triceps, sulek and lateral each got one from the same session. Press is the only lift from Friday's push still at 4 sets.
rationale.relationship: My best read is that chest going 3 to 4 sets on 8/7 gave the target a fourth slot that a 4-rep set fails, killing the whole grade — but the target list isn't saved with your sessions, so I can't verify that and you should treat it as a guess. What is not a guess: your best press scored zero and set count was the only thing that changed. Withdrawal clause stands — if the next upper day produces a press row with four sets logged and no load change, my reading is wrong and I'll retire it.

suggestions.predict: Run three sets, or four honest ones, and 250 produces a press feed row on the next upper day and the ownership repeat can finally bank. Repeat Sunday's shape and I expect no press row again — a third session where the best press in your file counts for nothing.

suggestions.title: Check the ham machine actually makes 125 before you debut it — the hack number went wrong exactly this way

rationale.science: Progressive overload only reads as progress if the load on the record is the load that was moved; a debut onto a rung that doesn't physically exist corrupts the lift's history rather than advancing it (Article IX — never let an instrument report what wasn't measured).
rationale.data: Ham 125 is queued live and undone (q_ham_125, state DEBUT), earned honestly off 120 x 12,12,11 — four reps clear of last time against your own measured spread of 2.7. Your app filed the question itself on 8/10: 'does this machine actually make 125 next? If not, fix the ladder in SETUP.' Separately on the same day, hack had to be record-corrected from a filed 160 to the 180 x 9,9,10 you actually did, because the weight editor only walked the ladder already on file.
rationale.relationship: Same failure mode, one day apart: the app can only offer rungs it already knows about, so an unverified ladder either blocks a load you can do or debuts one you can't. Thirty seconds in SETUP before the next lower day is the whole fix.

suggestions.predict: Confirm or correct the rung and the 125 debut runs against a real number, and hack's reps-are-the-ladder rule holds cleanly at the 180 top. Skip it and the next lower day either stalls on a rung that isn't there or files a load you didn't move.
